entry_points.answer: TicketService.request / read / purchase, called once per user action; purchase may be retried by the client.

untrusted_input.question: Q1
untrusted_input.answer: The user name and the timing of calls come from clients; the stock comes from the operator and is trusted.

input_size.answer: No byte input: the inputs are a user name and the order of calls; the stock is at most a few hundred tickets per event.

expected_outcomes.answer: 'sold_out' and 'no_request' are answers, not failures; a retry returns the first answer.

refused_resources.question: Q2
refused_resources.answer: A purchase that cannot get the database lock within 30 seconds raises; it must not answer success.

properties.answer: NoOversell, StockNonNegative, Conservation, SoldNeverDecreases, and every request is eventually answered.

questions.question: Which inputs to the ticket service come from clients you do not trust?
questions.answer: User names and call timing come from clients; the stock is set by the operator.

questions.question: When SQLite stays locked past the 30-second timeout, should a purchase raise rather than answer?
questions.answer: Raise. It must never answer success without the reservation.

targets.promise: No more tickets are sold than the event had, whatever order concurrent purchases and retries run in.
targets.harm: Two buyers pay for one seat and one of them is turned away at the door.

anchors.quote: "UPDATE tickets SET remaining = remaining - 1 WHERE event_id = ? AND remaining > 0"

targets.why_tests_miss: The oversell needs two purchases interleaved between a read and a write; the seeded property test makes one call at a time and never interleaves inside purchase().
targets.why_first: Conservation and the idempotent retry both rest on the reservation being atomic; it is the one place in tickets.py where the order of events decides the outcome.

tool.name: fvkit
tool.why: Whether events can happen in a bad order suits a model checker over a small model of the design; fvkit needs no install and its traces bind the model to this code.

scope.verified: the purchase protocol for two users and one ticket, every interleaving
scope.bounds: 2 users, stock 1 in the model; the property test widens to 4 users, stock 2
not_covered: refunds and cancellations (the service has none)

targets.next: entrance B — done in this example: model.yaml, source-map.yaml, code-first/modeling-brief.md

targets.promise: The existing property test fails whenever the service sells more than its stock or loses a ticket.
targets.harm: A regression in the reservation passes CI because the property test never fires.
targets.why_tests_miss: Nobody has seen these checks fail on broken code: a check that never failed proves nothing.
targets.route_reason: The design is verified in T1; this target makes the code's own test a check that can fail, so it guards every change between model runs.

tool.name: project-tests
tool.why: The repository already runs test_properties.py; fv props runs it with a one-line breakage per property.

scope.verified: NoOversell and Conservation are reached by 40 seeded schedules and fire on a one-line breakage each
assumptions: observe() reads the database, not the purchase code's return values
not_covered: StockNonNegative and SoldNeverDecreases have no breakage that fires them first

targets.promise: No purchase variant answers success after the stock is gone.
targets.harm: A buyer is told they have a ticket that does not exist.
targets.why_tests_miss: The check-then-act variant is only exercised by the negative control; nothing states what it promises.
targets.route_reason: A per-function contract with a probe shows the defect in the code itself; a second model of the same design would repeat T1.

tool.name: fvkit
tool.why: fv contracts checks the FM-Agent specs and re-runs each probe.

scope.verified: the behavioural specs of purchase, read and _purchase_check_then_act
scope.bounds: one probe per mismatch (stock 1, two users)
assumptions: the probe loads the service through its public module
not_covered: a MATCH is the agent's reasoning (E0), not a proof

notes: Written for the example: the answers and the maintainer are illustrative. harness.py is test tooling (role: tooling).
